criteria.text: The participant has histological or cytological confirmation of NSCLC.

The participant has Clinical Stage II-IIIB (N0, N1, N2) NSCLC treated with presurgical chemoimmunotherapy, with residual tumor present at time of surgery, and does not have a pathologic complete response.
The participant has Pathologic Stage II-IIIB (N0, N1, N2) NSCLC treated with initial upfront resection.
The participant has Clinical Stage III, unresectable NSCLC, without progression on concurrent platinum-based chemoradiotherapy.
The participant has disease with evidence of KRAS G12C mutation.
The participant has known programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression.
The participant has an ECOG performance status of 0 or 1.
The participant is able to swallow oral medication.
The participant has adequate laboratory parameters.
The participant's contraceptive use is consistent with local regulations for those participating in clinical studies.
The participant has a negative pregnancy test.
The participant is not breastfeeding during treatment.
The participant has known, actionable changes in the EGFR or ALK genes.
The participant has another type of cancer that is progressing or required active treatment within the past 2 years before screening.
The participant has an active autoimmune disease that required systemic treatment in the past 2 years.

The participant had any immune-related side effect or allergic reaction (Grade 3 or higher) from a previous immunotherapy medicine, or any immune-related side effect greater than Grade 1 that has not resolved, unless they have hormone-related diseases who are now on stable hormone replacement therapy.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: These questions are about the trial "Study of Olomorasib (LY3537982) in Combination With Standard of Care in Participants With Resected or Unresectable KRAS G12C-mutant Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer". Your earlier answers already covered 4 of its rules. I'll ask about the rest of its rules one at a time. You can skip any question, and "I don't know" is always fine.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. For this study, you need to have had chemotherapy and immunotherapy before surgery, and still have tumor cells found in the tissue after the operation. Did your surgery show that some tumor cells were still present?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I haven't had any surgery yet. They said the tumor is too big for an operation.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks for clarifying. Since you haven't had surgery, does your doctor say your cancer is Clinical Stage III and unresectable? Also, have you finished platinum-based chemoradiotherapy, and has the cancer stayed stable or improved without getting worse?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know what stage it is officially, but they said it's in my chest and lymph nodes. I haven't had any chemo or radiation yet.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had your tumor tested to see if it has a KRAS G12C mutation? This is a specific genetic change in the cancer cells. If you aren't sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No clue. I don't know if they tested for that specific mutation.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had your tumor tested to see if it has programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression? This is a test that looks at a specific protein on the cancer cells. If you aren't sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Some PD number? Didn't stick. I don't know what that means.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you able to swallow pills or capsules to take oral medication?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yeah, I can swallow pills fine. No trouble with that.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had any blood tests or lab work done in the last 2 weeks to check your overall health and organ function?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know. I haven't had any recent lab work done.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you currently use any form of birth control or contraception?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Ha. No. I'm a 66-year-old man, so that's not an issue for me.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been told that your cancer has changes in the EGFR or ALK genes? If you aren't sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Don't know. I haven't been told about any EGFR or ALK gene changes.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you ever had a severe (Grade 3 or higher) immune-related side effect or allergic reaction from an immunotherapy medicine, or any immune-related side effect greater than Grade 1 that hasn't resolved?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had any immunotherapy yet. I haven't started any treatment at all.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that's all my questions. Your record for this trial is ready, for you and your oncologist. They and the trial team decide whether it is right for you.
